answer: Sybil resistance couples identity bonding to detection-linked loss: when k identities coordinate equivocation, correlated penalties grow as O(k^2), so each added signer raises the aggregate slash and drains bonded escrow. Detection then applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the controlling stake, making swarm expansion economically hollow. A beacon supplies common evidence, while cryptographic attribution prevents an attacker from using forged proofs to escape.
